y1: The chief priests plotted to kill Jesus, saying, "Not during the feast, lest a riot occur among the people." Right then, in Bethany at the house of Simon the leper, a woman poured an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume on Jesus' head.
y2: The disciples were indignant, saying, "This could have been given to the poor." Jesus said, "She has done a good work for Me," and "She did it to prepare Me for burial." The woman was the first person to understand Jesus' death.
y3: "Christ" means "the anointed one." Oil was poured on the heads of kings. An unnamed woman, not a priest, anointed King Jesus. That King would take His throne on the cross.
y5: Immediately after this, Judas Iscariot, "one of the twelve," went to the chief priests and asked, "What are you willing to give me?" They weighed out thirty pieces of silver for him.
y6: Thirty pieces of silver was the compensation for a slave gored to death by an ox in {Exodus 21:32}. It also appears as the "wages of the shepherd" in {Zechariah 11:12–13}. While the woman poured perfume worth more than 300 denarii, Judas sold Jesus for a tenth of that price.
y7: The Bible does not detail Judas's motives. Money ({John 12:6}), disappointment regarding the Messiah, and Satan's influence ({Luke 22:3}) are mentioned. The important thing is this: even if you are with Jesus for three years, your heart can be somewhere else.
y8: The Meal of the New Covenant
y9: The Passover meal was a meal to remember the exodus from Egypt. When Jesus said, "One of you will betray Me," the disciples asked one by one, "Lord, is it I?" But Judas said, "Rabbi, is it I?"
y10: Jesus broke the bread and said, "Take, eat; this is My body." Then He gave the cup and said, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins." Jesus Himself stood in the place of the Passover lamb of the exodus.
y11: The other disciples said "Lord" (kyrios), but Judas said "Rabbi." In the Gospel of Matthew, Judas is the only disciple who calls Jesus "Rabbi." Even though they sat at the same table, their confessions were different.
y13: While singing a hymn and going to the Mount of Olives, Jesus quoted {Zechariah 13:7}: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered." At the same time, He made a promise: "After I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee."
y14: Peter said, "Even if everyone leaves You, I will never leave You," but Jesus said, "Tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." All the disciples said, "Even if we must die with You, we will not deny You," but that night they all fled.
y15: Jesus gave the promise to meet again (in Galilee) "before" the disciples stumbled. Even knowing their failure, He does not cut off the relationship. In 28:7 and 10, this promise is fulfilled exactly.
verse: "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins."
prayer: Jesus, thank You for Your love in giving Your body and blood unsparingly for me, even though You were sold for thirty pieces of silver. Let me let go of the thirty pieces of silver in my heart and pour out my most precious thing like that woman. I trust in You, who holds me before I stumble, even when I am weak like Peter. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: perfume. Mark says it was worth more than 300 denarii, which was a laborer's wages for a year. She broke the jar and poured it all out. The Gospel of John says this woman was Mary, the sister of Lazarus ({John 12:3}).
d1: Judas. "Iscariot" may mean "man of Kerioth." He might have been the only disciple from Judea among the twelve. Although his name means "praise," he chose the path of betrayal.
d2: Passover. Death "passed over" the houses where the blood of the lamb was smeared on the doorframes ({Exodus 12}). Jesus dies as the Passover lamb ({1 Corinthians 5:7}). In Azerbaijani, "Pasxa" also refers to Easter.
d3: covenant. The Sinai covenant was made with animal blood ({Exodus 24:8}). Jesus makes the "new covenant" of {Jeremiah 31:31} with His own blood. The name "New Testament" (New Covenant) comes from this.
d4: deny. It is the same verb as in "let him deny himself" in 16:24. Peter will deny Jesus instead of himself. See also the verse "whoever denies Me before men" in 10:33.
